items.note: The page turns $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ into the chirp convolution by citing the linked Bluestein page. It then derives $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$ in the paper's order (unit substitution, tensoring, commuting with pointwise products, the two normalizations), which matches the proof of Lemma chirp-permutation (paper lines 3938-3983).

dropped: the periodicity of $a$ with period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$ (which is where $t_i$ even is used); the page says $t_i$ is even but never says $a$ is periodic
the definition of the target permutation $(P_{t_i}v)_k=v_{-s_ik}$, which gives the identity its meaning
items.note: Stated with a link to the Bluestein page, as the assignment asks: $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot u)}{T}$, with $a$ as in the paper (line 3917). It is not derived here, correctly, since another page derives it.

The page writes out the sum $\frac1q\sum_k z_{ck}e^{2\pi ikj/q}=\frac1q\sum_h z_he^{2\pi ihc^{-1}j/q}=(R_c^{-1}F_q^+z)_j$, justifies the substitution ('which permutes the residues because $c$ is a unit'), identifies $R=\bigotimes_iR_{t_i}$, and tensors to get $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=R^{-1}F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$ and $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$. All of this is correct and follows the paper (lines 3953-3962).

The page gives $(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)=R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$, then $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}[R(\cdot)]=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}(\cdot)$ by the previous identity. Using $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, it gets $\frac1SF^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=\frac{u*v}{S^2}$, exactly as in the paper (lines 3963-3982).

errors.quote: The source permutation is $R=\bigotimes_i P_{s_i}$ with $(P_{s_i}u)_j=u_{t_ij}$, and the target permutation is $Q=\bigotimes_i P_{t_i}$.
errors.problem: The page defines $P_{s_i}$ but not $P_{t_i}$. By analogy a reader would take $(P_{t_i}v)_k=v_{s_ik}$. The paper defines $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$ (line 3557), and that minus sign is what makes the chirp identity hold with the negative-sign $F_{\boldsymbol t}$: '$Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform' (line 3951).
